en: Ice left outside on a hot sunny day in Manila melts into liquid water because heat increases molecular motion.
Iron gates in coastal towns like Cebu rust faster because salt in the sea air accelerates the chemical reaction.
Seawater is a homogeneous mixture because dissolved salt crystals are evenly distributed throughout the liquid ocean water.
Morning fog on Mount Pulag forms when cooled atmospheric water vapor condenses into visible liquid water droplets.
Pumice stones found near Taal Volcano float on lake water because trapped gas bubbles make them less dense than water.
Fallen mangoes rotting on the ground undergo a chemical change as bacteria break them down into entirely new substances.
Warm air rising above a beach fire expands because heat causes the gas molecules to move faster and spread apart.
Muddy floodwater from a typhoon is a heterogeneous mixture where solid soil particles are temporarily suspended in liquid water.
Liquid coconut water freezes into solid ice when placed inside a freezer because dropping temperatures slow molecular movement.
Green banana peels turn yellow as enzymes trigger chemical changes that break down chlorophyll during the ripening process.
Sugar dissolves much faster in hot calamansi juice than in cold water because higher temperatures increase molecular movement.
Frost forming on cold grass in Baguio is an example of deposition, where water vapor turns directly into solid ice.
